before.title: 1.2 Petrol Valve Cotter Defect — Engine Destruction (DVSA Recall)
before.description: Clio III 1.2 petrol engines built between 17 September and 30 November 2010 were recalled (DVSA reference R/2011/118) because out-of-specification valve cotters could let a valve drop into the cylinder, destroying the engine. 3,308 UK cars were affected. An unremedied car can suffer sudden, catastrophic engine failure with no warning, writing off the engine.
before.solution: The recall remedy is free replacement of the valve cotters by a Renault dealer; owners of 2010-2011 1.2 Clios should check the recall status by VIN on the GOV.UK recall checker. If the failure has already occurred, the engine requires rebuild or replacement.
symptoms: Sudden loud metallic noise from the engine
Immediate engine stall and failure to restart

before.title: 1.5 dCi EGR Valve Sticking and Clogging
before.description: The EGR valve on the 1.5 dCi clogs with soot and carbon, sticking open or closed — a fault so common on this engine that Renault specialists describe 1.5 dCis as suffering 'big time' with EGR problems, and Delphi published a dedicated repair guide for it. A valve stuck open causes rough running, black smoke, and hesitation; stuck closed it raises exhaust gas temperatures, which Honest John forum experts link to consequential turbo bearing failures. The fault commonly logs P2413 (EGR system performance) and recurs if the carbon-packed EGR housing is not also cleaned.
before.solution: Remove and thoroughly clean the EGR valve and its housing of carbon; if the valve is physically worn or its tip has broken off, replace it. Persistent codes after replacement point to EGR wiring, vacuum lines, or the position sensor, which should be checked before fitting another valve.
symptoms: Hesitation or jerky running under load

before.title: 1.5 dCi (K9K) Fuel Injector and Injection Pump Failure
before.description: The 1.5 dCi K9K diesel suffers well-documented fuel injector failures, often triggered by injection pump wear or fuel contamination that sends metal debris through the common-rail system into the injectors. Honest John documented a 2007 Clio 1.5 dCi whose injection pump broke up and sent shards into the injectors, with a repair quote of over £3,600 plus VAT. Owners report sequential injector failures, 'injection fault' dash warnings, power loss, and no-start conditions; once the rail is contaminated, the pump, rail, and all four injectors typically need replacing together.
before.solution: Replace the failed injector(s) with units coded to the ECU and renew the fuel filter; some injectors can be professionally refurbished. If the high-pressure pump has shed debris, the accepted fix is replacing the pump, rail, and all four injectors and flushing the fuel system, otherwise contamination causes repeat failures.
symptoms: Engine shuddering or rough running at idle
Glow plug warning light staying on

before.title: EDC Dual-Clutch Gearbox Judder, TCU Faults and Clutch Failure
before.description: Clio IV models with the six-speed EDC automatic (the dry-clutch Getrag DCT250, the same family as the troubled DSG/PowerShift units) suffer low-speed judder, jerky 1st-2nd shifts, clunks engaging Drive or Reverse, overheating warnings in traffic, and 'Check auto gearbox' messages. Causes range from TCU (transmission control unit) software and module faults — which Renault addressed on some cars — to worn dry-clutch friction surfaces and slow actuators. One documented Clio RS 200 EDC failure drew a quote of about $4,500 for the clutch pack alone.
before.solution: First step is a dealer software update with clutch touch-point relearn and adaptive reset, which cures many judder complaints; TCU replacement fixed others under Renault goodwill. Worn clutch packs or mechatronic faults require replacement of the clutch pack or repair of the mechatronic unit at a gearbox specialist.
symptoms: Judder or shudder when pulling away
Clunking when engaging Drive or Reverse
Gearbox overheating warning in stop-start traffic

before.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Column Failure
before.description: The electrically assisted steering column on the Clio III (2005-2012) is a notorious failure point: UK steering specialists describe complete column failure as 'a very common fault', caused by poor ground connections to the EPS motor or internal failure of the column's motor and control unit (fault code C1608). Assistance becomes intermittently heavy — sometimes in one direction only — before failing completely, leaving the car drivable but very heavy to steer. The problem resurfaced on the Clio V: a February 2020 EU/DVSA recall covered 2019-built cars for internal failure of the steering column motor control causing loss of assistance while driving.
before.solution: Clean and remake the EPS motor ground connections first; if the column itself has failed, fit a remanufactured or repaired EPS column (around £800 plus VAT and coding for a new unit; remanufactured units are cheaper). Clio V owners should check the DVSA/EU recall status and have the column replaced free by Renault if affected.
symptoms: Steering goes heavy intermittently, sometimes in one direction
'STOP' and steering fault message with total loss of assistance
Vibration through the wheel when turning

before.title: Keycard Not Detected / Card Reader Failure
before.description: Clio III and IV keycard models commonly refuse to start with a 'key card not detected' message. The flexible credit-card-style keycards are bent, sat on, and dropped, eventually killing the internal chip — UK auto locksmiths note both 3- and 4-button cards have a known chip failure — while the in-dash card reader and its antenna ring can also fail and mimic a bad card. Dealership replacement of a single coded card runs roughly €250-400, so owners frequently chase the wrong component without proper diagnosis.
before.solution: Fit a fresh CR2032 battery first, then have a diagnostic check confirm whether the reader actually detects card insertion before buying anything. Replace the failed keycard (auto locksmiths are far cheaper than dealers) or, if the reader is at fault, replace the card reader module.
symptoms: 'Key card not detected' message on the dash
Car fails to start even with a new card battery
Intermittent recognition — card works after reinsertion or wiggling
